prompt:
Create a realistic production-quality editorial WEBSITE design for Missional by Design, edge to edge, 1440 pixels wide by 2000 pixels tall, showing a continuous homepage and several sections. Crisp readable UI text, no browser or device frame, no concept labels. Audience: Christian technologists and ministry/product leaders. The offer connects Christian purpose, changing context and practical design. Preserve the approved rock specimen from reference image 1: the same broad fractured outline and reflective pale icy blue-silver faces. No new rock silhouette, dents, tiny gravel texture, glass crystal, physical cross cutout or biblical props. A sharp four-point optical reflection with slight local glow is part of this identity. Reference images 2 and 3 are quality benchmarks for confident hierarchy, human photography and editorial rhythm, not brands/layouts to copy. Reference image 4 provides an approved fictional startup working scene. Use no fabricated testimonials, endorsements or performance statistics. Small captions identify generated editorial imagery. At most two type families; readable body type, restrained structural devices, no repetitive cards, excessive labels or large black slabs. One primary action. Navigation reads Principles, Canvas, Patterns, Writing, About, EN / DE. Wordmark: missional — by — design, with two short rules around by. Show real text in every visible section. Current date is 16 October 2026; no dates are needed.
Art direction: a lively, exceptionally crafted independent publication at the intersection of Christian practice, urban culture and technology. Human-first, bright white, confident modern sans-serif display, occasional elegant serif for a reflective question, deep blue and restrained warm colour drawn from the photographs. Lead with a large candid colour startup-workshop photograph from reference 4, integrated with a clear headline and one primary action as a unified editorial opening. Keep the text in clean readable space; image and text should feel art-directed together, never a stock photo card beside a text column. Headline: “Faithful design starts with people.” Deck: “Tools for Christian teams discerning what to build and how to serve.” Primary action: “Explore the approach”. Immediately follow with “Our context changes. Our listening continues.” and the exact question “What really is the good news in our context?” Bring the approved neighborhood/rock image from reference 1 into this section, large enough to recognise the exact specimen and its optical reflection. Then make the resource tangible with a compact editorial feature “From conviction to a design decision” and three distinct readable entry links: “Ten principles”, “The missional canvas”, “Bible & faith patterns”. Use varying composition and strong spatial rhythm, short genuine descriptions and a human invitation to read further. Preserve a clear quiet reading layer. No glossy SaaS cards, no grid of identical sculptures, no dense manifesto or gratuitous icon badges.
Use photographs and faces ONLY from reference 4 or new fictional people, never copy people from comparator screenshots 2 and 3. Missional by Design is an open RESOURCE by Tobias Treppmann, not an established membership community; do not invent community size, offices, locations, events, affiliations or group claims. Render only the supplied short copy and truthful resource descriptions.
